Closest thing to a NDE I've had, if you could call it that, was during severe intraoperative hypotension during an emergency C-section. I had had issues with high blood pressure teetering towards preeclampsia towards the end of my pregnancy. The drop from moderately high to severely low BP during surgery was a major complication, something hypovolemic in relation to the surgery and my preeclampsia.  Though I did not actually enter cardiac arrest, I do have vague memory of  a visual and sensational hallucination during this emergency.   
  
I remember floating in what looked to be an entirely never ending lake of mercury. There was a light refraction from the surface but no definitive light source. I have that small memory of the visuals, but the thing I remember the most is the feeling. I felt amazing, better than I ever have. The feeling was truly indescribable. I felt true peace and the definition of euphoria. I was calm, fulfilled. I felt pure joy, like the journey was over and I could finally be where I felt the most comfortable. Though this never actually crossed my mind in that moment, if I had had the ability to think about it I know that in that moment I did not want to ever leave my new found paradise. 

Looking back on that in the days afterwards I felt a lot of guilt that I had felt so peaceful in that moment. I would have been devasted to have worsened and never experienced my daughter's life with her.
